body.statement: Almost surely, the constrained and unconstrained GCM slopes differ only on a finite contact interval at every \(x\), the integral \(D(x)\) is finite and nonnegative, and \(D\) has a separable locally bounded stationary version. Moreover, the joint contact radius for all \(x\) in a bounded interval has a tail sufficient for independent truncation of well-separated Brownian blocks.
body.justification: The continuum maximum and any declustering rule are meaningful only after the nonlocal GCM energy is localized and given a separable version.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) prove the one-point LR integral is well defined; the uniform contact-radius and local-boundedness statement for the translated field is not supplied there.
body.consumer: Finite-dimensional stationarity is available, while simulation and block separation still need separability and a quantitative common contact-radius tail.

obligation.what_is_open: A separable locally bounded version of the LR field and a quantitative common contact-radius tail for all constraint locations in a compact interval have not been constructed.
obligation.obstruction: Cubic-exponential localization of tilted argmin vertices does not exclude a remote supporting chord that changes either one-sided constrained GCM. The target's phrase concerning a tail sufficient for block independence also lacks a quantitative threshold to verify.
obligation.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity. A Gaussian reflection and union-bound argument gives a cubic-exponential tail for every bounded family of tilted argmin vertices, thereby isolating remote supporting chords as the remaining geometric event.
obligation.partial_result:
The available exact property is finite-dimensional stationarity.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
 \mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x).
\]
Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the change of variable \(s=x+t\) give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy whenever that energy is defined.  Stationarity of Brownian increments therefore implies
\[
 (D(x_1+h),\ldots,D(x_m+h))
 \stackrel{d}{=}(D(x_1),\ldots,D(x_m))
\]
for every finite collection \(x_1,ldots,x_m\) and every \(h\in\mathbb R\).

One can also localize ordinary tilted argmin vertices.  For each fixed \(C<\infty\), Gaussian reflection bounds on every interval \([j,j+1]\), followed by a summable union bound, give constants \(c_1,c_2,R_0>0\) such that
\[
 \Pr\!\left{exists |c|\le C:\
   \operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in\mathbb R}\{X(t)-ct\}
   \not\subset[-R,R]\right}
 \le c_1e^{-c_2R^3},
 \qquad R\ge R_0.
\]
Indeed, for \(R\ge2C\), a minimizing point with \(|t|\ge R\) must satisfy \(W(t)\le-t^2/2\), because the value at zero is zero.  On \([j,j+1]\), this event is contained in the union of \(\{W(j)\le-j^2/4\}\) and \(\{\inf_{0\le r\le1}[W(j+r)-W(j)]\le-j^2/4\}\), whose probabilities are bounded respectively by constants times \(e^{-c j^3}\) and \(e^{-c j^4}\); summing over \(j\ge R-1\) and treating the negative half-line identically proves the display.  The same argument also gives \(W(t)/t^2\to0\) almost surely and hence coercivity of every bounded linear tilt.

This vertex bound does not control a remote supporting chord of either one-sided constrained GCM.  Consequently it neither proves that the constrained and unconstrained slopes have jointly compact difference support uniformly over a continuum of constraint locations nor constructs a separable locally bounded version of \(D\).
